statement: The function returns a result r and r is the bitwise XOR of all len(nums1)*len(nums2) integers of the form nums1[i] XOR nums2[j], where 0 <= i < len(nums1) and 0 <= j < len(nums2). The XOR over these integers is taken in any order; it is well-defined because bitwise XOR is associative and commutative.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every nums1 and nums2 satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, go out of bounds, or overflow.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r < 2^30, i.e. 0 <= r < 1073741824.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0.

statement: Let X2 be nums2[0] XOR nums2[1] XOR ... XOR nums2[len(nums2)-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = X2.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000; len(nums2) is even; len(nums1) is odd.

statement: Let X1 be nums1[0] XOR nums1[1] XOR ... XOR nums1[len(nums1)-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = X1.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000; len(nums1) is even; len(nums2) is odd.

statement: For any two slices b and b' of 64-bit integers such that len(b) = len(b') = len(nums2) and every element of b and b' is between 0 and 1000000000, if xor_all_nums(nums1,b) returns r and xor_all_nums(nums1,b') returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000; len(nums1) is even.

statement: For any two slices a and a' of 64-bit integers such that len(a) = len(a') = len(nums1) and every element of a and a' is between 0 and 1000000000, if xor_all_nums(a,nums2) returns r and xor_all_nums(a',nums2) returns r', then r = r'.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000; len(nums2) is even.

statement: If xor_all_nums(nums1,nums2) returns r and xor_all_nums(nums2,nums1) returns r', then r = r'.

statement: Let p be any slice of the same length as nums1 such that p is a permutation of nums1, meaning that for every integer v the number of indices i with p[i] = v equals the number of indices i with nums1[i] = v, and every element of p is between 0 and 1000000000. If xor_all_nums(nums1,nums2) returns r and xor_all_nums(p,nums2) returns r', then r = r'.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every integer k with 0 <= k < 64, the k-th least-significant bit of r is 1 if and only if the number of pairs (i,j) with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= j < len(nums2), and the k-th bit of nums1[i] XOR nums2[j] equal to 1, is odd. The k-th bit of a non-negative integer x is (x >> k) mod 2.
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let X1 be nums1[0] XOR nums1[1] XOR ... XOR nums1[len(nums1)-1], and let X2 be nums2[0] XOR nums2[1] XOR ... XOR nums2[len(nums2)-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = ((if len(nums2) is odd then X1 else 0) XOR (if len(nums1) is odd then X2 else 0)).

statement: Let X1 be nums1[0] XOR nums1[1] XOR ... XOR nums1[len(nums1)-1], and let X2 be nums2[0] XOR nums2[1] XOR ... XOR nums2[len(nums2)-1]. Whenever the function returns a result r, r = X1 XOR X2. (This completes the case table of spec_4, spec_5, spec_6: both odd is the only remaining parity combination.)
preconditions: len(nums1) and len(nums2) are between 1 and 100000 inclusive; for every i with 0 <= i < len(nums1), 0 <= nums1[i] <= 1000000000; for every j with 0 <= j < len(nums2), 0 <= nums2[j] <= 1000000000; len(nums1) is odd; len(nums2) is odd.

statement: Let p be any slice with len(p) = len(nums2) that is a permutation of nums2 (for every integer v, the number of indices j with p[j] = v equals the number of indices j with nums2[j] = v) and whose elements are all between 0 and 1000000000. If xor_all_nums(nums1,nums2) returns r and xor_all_nums(nums1,p) returns r', then r = r'. (Symmetric counterpart of spec_10, which only covers reordering nums1.)
